task: Review every supplied part, discover the most consequential events from the supplied evidence, cluster related reports, assign the best-fit broad news category dynamically and produce up to 150 processed stories using schema/processed-news.schema.json. The final portfolio must contain at least five well-supported stories in every category. Treat social attention as a discovery signal rather than verification. More than half of the final stories must originate with independent, local or social discovery, using the first source in each story as the discovery source; established outlets may account for no more than half.

items.title: Supreme Court stays probe against Pinarayi Vijayan for a week in CMRL case; asks HC to hear his appeal
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Wednesday stayed the investigation against former Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan in the CMRL-Exalogic case [ Pinarayi Vijayan v Adv KM Shajahan & ors ]. The stay will operate for a week to enable Vijayan to pursue an appeal before a division bench of the Kerala High Court against a single-judge's direction to register FIR against him in the case. The vacation bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana today took exception to the High Court acting in haste and directing registration of a first information report (FIR) against Vijayan based on the Enforcement Directorate's (ED) recommendation. The Court noted that the State had already constituted a special investigation team (SIT) to conduct a preliminary enquiry and hence, the High Court should not have acted in haste and ordered an FIR without hearing Vijayan. The Court also cautioned the ED against meddling into the domain of other probe agencies. "The FIR is registered. That is it. We will allow the FIR to exist, but we will stall the investigation. items.title: When the body bears witness: How Chennai’s heat affects the health of poor women
items.summary: Every day, 39-year-old Selvi sits by the roadside on Nungambakkam to sell flowers. An umbrella makes a feeble attempt to shield her from Chennai’s scorching sun. The heat is unbearable, and so are the headaches she gets during the summers. But staying hydrated is not an option for her. “I don’t drink much water to avoid having to use the toilet,” she said. There are no toilets near the spot where she sells flowers. “Even if I take a short break to use the toilet, my flowers get stolen. It has happened a couple of times,” she explained. She finally drinks water only after reaching her home in the Washermanpet slum late in the evening. The day inevitably takes a toll on her. “By evening, my whole body hurts. I get unbearable headaches on summer days, but I don’t have them when it rains. I have also had vaginal infections a couple of times,” she said. For poor women in parts of urban and coastal Chennai, the summer arrives with a number of health issues.
